domain: Visitor identity resolution and behavioral tracking
summary: The first-party spine is real: visitor_sessions/visitor_events with a BEFORE-INSERT scoring trigger, a 15-min hot-lead cron registered in vercel.json:88, a signed-token email tracking layer used by 11 distinct send paths, and a CRM contact page that renders CMAs/BPOs/engagement/behavior from live data. But the prior audit was too generous on three "have" items. Verified new defects it missed: (1) the KB tracker is mounted on ~60 page families (not just homepage/city/community) and every one of its events is dropped for a missing consent field — AND even if consent were fixed it sends `scrollDepth`/`section` keys the route never reads (it reads `scrollDepthPct`), so it is a three-layer break, not a one-line omission; (2) NOTHING anywhere writes a `search` or `cta_click` visitor_event, and `categorizePage` still matches `/search|/listings|/properties` which next.config.ts:149-151 permanently redirects to `/homes-for-sale` — so the search scoring branch, the `topSearches` panel, and the `active searcher` + `price-drop watcher` intent signals are structurally dead, not merely sparse; (3) `email_click` timeline rows are explicitly FILTERED OUT of the CRM timeline (crm/[id]/page.tsx:379), so the clicked URL is not "buried in a payload" — it is not rendered anywhere. The ad-targeting item is more live than reported: a second Meta Custom Audience ("RR Westside Bend Homeowners", id 120244510092910698) is pushed by scripts/meta-refresh-westside-audience.mjs which pushes LIVE by default and never consults META_AUDIENCE_PUSH_ENABLED. Separately, resolvePersonIdentity joins visitor_sessions on `fub_person_id = fub_legacy_id` while visitor-backfill writes the NATIVE crm_people.id into that same column — an id-space mismatch that can silently orphan a contact's whole session history.

items.requirement: Title-company dataset of skip-traced West Side Bend homeowners loaded into CRM
items.evidence: scripts/_westside-insert-netnew.mjs:74-88 inserts into crm_people via `sb.from('crm_people').insert(...)`, links parcels back by person_id, and writes reversal ids to out/westside-netnew-inserted-ids.json. 20 westside scripts present (scripts/westside-bend-enrich-batchdata.mjs, -realtor-filter.mjs, -local-enrich.mjs, -geo-assign.mjs, -seller-score.mjs, plus _westside-* audit/reconcile/strip helpers). scripts/meta-refresh-westside-audience.mjs:5-9 documents westside_parcels at 17,665 rows joined to crm_people on person_id.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Import mechanism is real and confirmed at the insert call site, not just the filename. Adding what the prior audit did not note: the whole pipeline is manual Node CLI — nothing in vercel.json refreshes it, and the insert is gated behind an explicit --apply flag, so drift between the title dataset and crm_people is silent. Live row counts and dedup state are not checkable from source.
items.why_it_matters: This is the seed population the entire run-ads-at-known-people and resolve-on-visit workflow depends on.

items.requirement: Run Facebook ads at these known people (Custom Audience targeting)

(a) lib/meta/audienceUpload.ts syncCrmAudience → CRM_AUDIENCE_NAME 'Ryan Realty CRM Leads', double-gated: lib/meta-env.ts:isMetaAudiencePushEnabled requires the exact string 'true' AND dryRun:false; app/api/cron/meta-audience-sync/route.ts:52-56 sets `const dryRun = !live`. Registered vercel.json:180, daily 0 9 * * *. META_AUDIENCE_PUSH_ENABLED is absent from .env.local. (b) scripts/meta-refresh-westside-audience.mjs — hardcoded AUDIENCE_ID '120244510092910698' ("RR Westside Bend Homeowners"), reads META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN, and its header documents "the first two pushes" already happened (one-time CSV 2026-05-25, then a fixed 7-key push 2026-07-09). Dry-run is OPT-IN (`--dry-run`); the default path pushes live.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the prior audit claimed nothing may ever have reached a live Meta audience and framed this as one flag-gated cron. Wrong — a second, already-populated live audience exists and bypasses the flag entirely.] The real gap is architectural, not on/off: the audience that is actually live (westside) is refreshed only by a hand-run script with no cron, no ledger row, and no suppression-drain leg, while the audience with the full compliance machinery (crm_people, suppression exclusion, removal queue, meta_audience_log ledger) is the one stuck in dry-run. That is backwards — the live list is the less-governed one. Whether META_AUDIENCE_PUSH_ENABLED is true in Vercel prod is still unknowable from source; it is NOT set locally.
items.why_it_matters: The list Matt is actually targeting today is maintained by a manual script whose compliance exclusions were bolted on later, while the governed daily path may be pushing nothing.

items.requirement: Resolve an anonymous visitor to the known CRM person on ad click, site visit, or email open
items.evidence: Email-click: app/actions/identity-bridge.ts:46-75 (identifyPersonFromEmailClick via ?_fuid, identifyPersonFromEmailClickNative via ?_pid), also served for raw-HTML docs by app/api/track/e/identify/route.ts + public/rr-doc-tracker.js. Sign-in: components/layout/VisitTrackerWithSession.tsx calls identifyAuthenticatedSession once per browser session. Both land in lib/visitor-backfill.ts backfillSessionToFub:141-287 → sets identified_at, crm_person_id AND fub_person_id, stamps prior events. stitchVisitorIdentity:56-112 upserts visitor_identity_map on rr_vid (cookie set in middleware.ts) and back-fills sibling sessions by rr_vid. Ad click: app/api/meta-capi/route.ts sends hashed PII forward only; grep for `_pid=`/`_fuid=` across lib, scripts, app returns zero hits in any Meta/ad-build path.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor missed a live id-space defect that breaks resolution even on the paths it called working.] lib/data/crm/resolvePersonIdentity.ts:180-190 resolves a contact's sessions with `.eq('fub_person_id', fubLegacyId)` and gates the identity_map OR-filter on `fub_person_id.eq.${fubLegacyId}` — but lib/visitor-backfill.ts:202 writes the NATIVE crm_people.id into that same fub_person_id column. For any contact whose crm_people.id differs from fub_legacy_id, or any post-cutover contact where fubLegacyId is null, session resolution falls back to email-only and can return zero sessions — silently emptying ContactBehaviorPanel, topListingsViewed and every intent signal. It also never queries visitor_sessions.crm_person_id, the column the visitors dashboard keys on. Separately, the auditor's ad-click finding is CONFIRMED: no per-person ad URL, no fbclid→person join, and visitor_identity_map is never read at track time to stamp a returning known visitor's new session — so a known homeowner clicking a FB ad is resolved only retroactively in the CRM, and only if the id-space join above happens to line up.
items.why_it_matters: Matt's core value is ads at known people plus resolve on click. The ad-click leg is structurally absent, and the legs that do exist rest on a join key that is written in one id space and read in another.

items.requirement: Track full session behavior: pages viewed, listings viewed, searches run
items.evidence: components/VisitTracker.tsx:236-240 fires page_view/listing_view through fireVisitorEvent → /api/visitors/track on every non-admin pathname change; mounted via components/layout/PublicClientLayer.tsx:51 (VisitTrackerWithSession), rendered from app/layout.tsx:148 and NOT wrapped in HideOnLP, so it runs site-wide. detectListing (VisitTracker.tsx:59-73) correctly parses both /listing/{key} and canonical /homes-for-sale/.../{street}-{mls}. supabase/migrations/20260522180000_visitor_tracking.sql:184-224 defines visitor_score_delta_for_event + the BEFORE-INSERT visitor_event_score_trigger.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor marked this "have" with "none for page or listing views themselves" and never checked searches, which it also listed under this requirement.] Page and listing views are genuinely wired. Searches are NOT. Grep across app/components/lib finds ZERO producers of `eventType: 'search'` or `'cta_click'` — both are in ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES (route.ts:170) and both carry score weights (search=3, cta_click=20) that can never fire from the Next.js site. Worse, VisitTracker.tsx:79 categorizes search pages with /^\/(search|listings|properties)/ — next.config.ts:149-151 makes all three PERMANENT redirects to /homes-for-sale, which matches no branch and falls through to 'other' (1 point). So the actual search surface is scored as a generic page view with no search page_category and no intent tag. components/GlobalIntentTracker.tsx (mounted alongside VisitTracker at PublicClientLayer.tsx:52) fires call_initiated/email_agent/form_start through lib/tracking.ts trackEvent — GA4 only, never /api/visitors/track — so high-intent CTA behavior also never reaches the CRM-linked store.
items.why_it_matters: This is the base signal everything downstream depends on, and one third of it (search + CTA intent) is silently absent from the store the CRM actually reads.

items.requirement: Track scroll depth and drop-off point on the site
items.evidence: components/listing/ListingTracker.tsx:56 and :72 fire scroll_depth only via lib/tracking.ts trackEvent (dataLayer/GA4/Meta pixel; read in full, no /api/visitors/track call). components/LandingPageTracker.tsx same pattern. components/site/kb/KbSectionTracker.client.tsx:14 builds `{ sessionId, eventType, pageUrl, ...extra }` — NO consent field; app/api/visitors/track/route.ts:239-247 coerces missing consent to 'declined' and returns `{ ok:true, dropped:true }` without writing. app/admin/(protected)/visitors/[sessionId]/page.tsx:111 and :134 render scroll_depth_pct. app/admin/(protected)/analytics/_lib/queries.ts:206-228 documents the D12 removal of per-milestone GA4 scroll data as fabricated.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor called this "partial" and blamed a one-line consent omission. It is worse on both axes.] First, blast radius: KbSectionTracker is mounted on roughly 60 page families — homepage, cities, communities, neighborhoods, subdivisions, zip, schools, parks, blog, guides, reports, housing-market, listing detail (app/listing/[listingKey]/page.tsx:571), and every LP via components/landing/LeadLandingPage.tsx:54 — not just "homepage and city/community pages." Every one is 100% dropped. Second, it is three bugs stacked, not one: even with consent added, internalTrack sends `scrollDepth` while route.ts:383 reads `body.scrollDepthPct`, and sends `section` which the route never maps into metadata — so scroll_depth rows would land with a NULL percentage (failing the >=75 scoring branch at migration line 192) and section_view rows would land with no section identity. Third, the file's own docblock records a PRIOR audit that fixed the pageUrl bug on these same lines and shipped without noticing the other three. Net: zero scroll or section data exists anywhere in visitor_events, the [sessionId] scroll column is permanently blank, and no per-page drop-off answer exists in the product. Calling this "partial" overstates it — the capability does not exist.
items.why_it_matters: Matt explicitly asked to be told where people drop off on a page. No surface answers that for any page, the plumbing meant to feed it has been broken through at least two audit cycles, and the one GA4 aggregate that remains is a single boolean across all LPs combined.

items.requirement: Deliverable tracking for newsletter, CMA, BPO, saved search and market report: delivered, opened, clicked, which listing clicked
items.evidence: lib/crm/attributed-links.ts:60 attributeOutbound is the single wrapper, and it is called from ELEVEN production paths (broader than the four claimed): lib/cma/send.ts:328, lib/bpo/send.ts:363, lib/crm/market-report-send.ts:159, lib/crm/bulk-handlers/email-cohort.ts:206, lib/newsletter/send-queue.ts:475, app/actions/contact-listing-matches.ts:156, app/actions/contact-cma.ts:306, app/actions/saved-search-alerts.ts:311, app/api/cma-drafts/[id]/send/route.ts:111. lib/email-tracking.ts signs HMAC tokens carrying personId/emailKey/url. app/api/track/e/click/route.ts:28-40 writes crm_timeline with body=target and payload.url=target, dedupe_key including the URL, then recordEmailEvent and recordNewsletterEngagement.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor said the data is captured but the UI only shows aggregate counts and a broker "would have to open the raw payload." The truth is harsher — the URL is not rendered at all.] app/admin/(protected)/crm/[id]/page.tsx:379 filters `t.kind !== 'email_open' && t.kind !== 'email_click' && t.kind !== 'sms_click'` OUT of timelineItems entirely; lines 290-299 collapse them into an opens/clicks integer pair attached to the email_out row. No component under components/admin/crm/ renders a click URL — ContactEmailEngagement.tsx contains no url/link reference. So "clicked these homes" is not a degraded view of existing UI, it is absent UI. The URL→MLS normalization the auditor flagged is also genuinely missing from lib/crm/email-events.ts. Capture is solid; presentation of the specific ask is missing.
items.why_it_matters: Matt asked specifically for clicked-these-homes as a timeline item. The data is in crm_timeline.body today and is deliberately suppressed from the only surface a broker reads.

items.requirement: Per-contact unified activity timeline on the CRM record
items.evidence: app/admin/(protected)/crm/[id]/page.tsx imports and RENDERS (not just imports) ContactCmaCard:633, ContactBpoCard:637, ContactBehaviorPanel:656, ContactEmailEngagement:665, ContactDeliveryPanel:668, ContactListingAlertsPanel:672, plus the crm_timeline feed at 378-395. Data comes from real DAL reads (getContactEmailEngagement at line 168, getContactBehaviorSummary).
items.gap: [VERIFIED] The assembly is real and every panel is reached in the render tree, not dead imports. But the auditor's "only gaps are upstream" framing undersells it: three of the panels are fed by pipelines this report downgrades. ContactBehaviorPanel's topSearches can never populate (no search event producer), its scroll signal never populates, and its whole session set depends on the resolvePersonIdentity fub_person_id/fub_legacy_id id-space mismatch. The shell is complete; the fill is thinner than the panel implies, and an empty panel reads to a broker as "this lead did nothing" rather than "we are not capturing this."
items.why_it_matters: This is the broker-sees-everything ask and the structure is genuinely built, but panels that silently render empty because of upstream breaks actively mislead.

items.requirement: Reports that are easy to read and drive action
items.evidence: app/admin/(protected)/analytics/funnel-breakdown/page.tsx:288 reads visitor_sessions directly (header lines 6-15 confirm no GA4 dependency); intent split, per-source stage drop-off, and an auto-generated insights block. Reachability CONFIRMED, which the auditor never checked: linked from app/admin/(protected)/analytics/_components/ReportCatalog.tsx:94 and app/admin/(protected)/reports/lead-flow/page.tsx:618. /admin/visitors/live linked from ReportCatalog.tsx:37, DashboardLeadPanel.tsx:50, ad-roi/page.tsx:503, and the daily digest email (app/api/cron/analytics-daily-digest/route.ts:275). Per-session journey linked from action-required/page.tsx:101,171,235.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Reachable, real-data, actionable for source efficiency and lead scoring. Cannot answer drop-off-at-a-scroll-position on a named page because no scroll data exists at all (see the scroll item, now downgraded to missing). Adding what the auditor omitted: the funnel's stage definitions inherit the broken intent taxonomy — sessions on the real search surface (/homes-for-sale) are bucketed 'other' rather than search, so the browsing-vs-buying split is skewed at the source, not just missing a scroll column.
items.why_it_matters: The report pattern is right; its inputs are miscategorized upstream and its most-requested dimension has no data behind it.

items.requirement: Intent scoring to infer starting-to-look or considering-selling
items.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260522180000_visitor_tracking.sql:158-179 (visitor_score_delta_for_event) and :184-224 (visitor_event_after_insert, BEFORE INSERT trigger created at :226-230) — real, DB-enforced. app/api/cron/visitor-hot-lead-escalation/route.ts:274-333 reads sessions at/above a configurable threshold and escalates; registered vercel.json:88 at */15. lib/data/crm/getContactBehaviorSummary.ts:166-215 deriveIntentSignals.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor wrote "none found. Real, reachable and database-enforced" — it did not check whether the inputs each scoring branch and each signal depends on are ever produced.] Of the 11 scoring branches, four are fed by nothing on the live site: `search` (no producer), `cta_click` (no producer — GlobalIntentTracker is GA4-only), `scroll_depth >= 75` (KB tracker 100% dropped, and would send the wrong key anyway), and `identify` (no eventType:'identify' producer found). The `page_category='search'` branch is also unreachable because next.config.ts:149-151 redirects /search, /listings and /properties to /homes-for-sale, which VisitTracker.tsx:79 does not match. Of the six deriveIntentSignals, `active searcher` (needs 3+ search events) and `price-drop watcher` (needs metadata.price_drop, written by nothing) can never fire. What genuinely works: listing_view=10, seller_intent=25, buyer_intent=15, financial_tools=10, area_guide=5, plus repeat-visitor, mortgage-calculator-user, home-value-seeker and the 5+-listings signal. Seller intent — Matt's headline use case — does work. Buyer intent is systematically underscored because the search surface scores 1 point instead of 3 and contributes no intent tag.
items.why_it_matters: The escalation cron is real and fires, but it fires on a score that undercounts every buyer whose behavior is searching rather than opening individual listings — the exact 'starting to look' signal Matt asked for.

shared_primitives_needed: A single client-side tracking dispatcher with a typed payload contract shared with app/api/visitors/track. Today four components (VisitTracker, KbSectionTracker, ListingTracker, LandingPageTracker, plus GlobalIntentTracker) each hand-roll a different partial payload; two of them omit consent entirely and one uses field names the route does not read. A shared typed emitter would have made all three KbSectionTracker bugs compile errors.

One canonical person→sessions resolver. resolvePersonIdentity joins on fub_person_id=fub_legacy_id, visitor-backfill writes crm_people.id into fub_person_id, and the visitors dashboard keys on crm_person_id — three readers, three different assumptions about the same join. Pick crm_person_id, migrate, and gate it.
A URL→listing-key resolver shared by the email click tracker, the CRM timeline renderer, and any future page report, so a destination URL consistently becomes a structured listing reference.

A single runtime flag-state surface (admin page or health cron) reporting which Meta/production flags are live vs dry-run. META_AUDIENCE_PUSH_ENABLED, META_CAPI_QUALIFIED_ENABLED and the westside script's implicit live-by-default posture are all invisible outside source code, and they disagree with each other.

An event-producer coverage gate. ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES lists search, cta_click and identify; nothing emits any of them, and the scoring function silently allocates weight to all three. A CI check asserting every allowed event type has at least one producer would have caught this.
open_questions_for_owner: The westside Meta audience (id 120244510092910698) is being refreshed by a hand-run script that pushes live by default and has no cron, no ledger, and a hand-copied version of the suppression logic. Do you want it folded into the governed daily meta-audience-sync cron, or is manual refresh intentional so you control push timing?

Is META_AUDIENCE_PUSH_ENABLED set to 'true' in Vercel production? It is not in .env.local, and nothing in the repo can tell us. If it is off, the CRM Leads audience has been computing and discarding a hashed population every morning at 09:00 UTC since it shipped.

For resolving an anonymous ad-clicker, are you willing to accept a signed per-person landing URL on ad creative (mirroring the existing _pid email mechanism)? Meta will not tell us server-side which audience member clicked, so this is the only join key available.

Do you want scroll/drop-off broken out per specific URL (e.g. 'the seller valuation LP loses 40% at 60% scroll')? Fixing the KB tracker is cheap, but a per-page drop-off report is new surface area — confirm it is worth building before we instrument for it.

Buyer-side scoring currently undercounts: a visitor browsing /homes-for-sale scores 1 point with no intent tag, while a single listing detail view scores 10. Should search-surface page views score as buyer intent, and at what weight?
